{{Short description|Model of emotion}}

[[File:Lövheim cube of emotion.svg|thumb|400px|Lövheim cube of emotion]]

'''Lövheim Cube of Emotion''' is a theoretical model for the relationship between the [[monoamine neurotransmitters]] [[serotonin]], [[dopamine]] and [[noradrenaline]] and [[emotion]]s. The model was presented in 2012 by Swedish researcher Hugo Lövheim.<ref>{{cite web | title = Motivation and emotion/Book/2015/Lövheim cube of emotion | url = https://en.wikiversity.org/w/index.php?title=Motivation_and_emotion/Book/2015/L%C3%B6vheim_cube_of_emotion&oldid=1595908 | date = 11 September 2016 | access-date = 11 September 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last = Lövheim | first = Hugo | title = A new three-dimensional model for emotions and monoamine neurotransmitters | journal = Medical Hypotheses | volume = 78 | issue = 2 | pages = 341–348 | publisher = Elsevier Ltd | date = 2012 | doi = 10.1016/j.mehy.2011.11.016 | pmid = 22153577}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Perry | first1 = Clint | last2 = Baciadonna | first2 = Luigi | title = Studying emotion in invertebrates: what has been done, what can be measured and what they can provide | journal = Journal of Experimental Biology | volume = 220 | issue = 21 | pages = 3856–3868 | publisher = The Company of Biologists | date = 2017 | doi = 10.1242/jeb.151308 | pmid = 29093185 | s2cid = 531311 | doi-access = free}}</ref>

==Overview==
Lövheim classifies emotions according to [[Silvan Tomkins]], and orders the basic emotions in a three-dimensional coordinate system where the level of the monoamine neurotransmitters form [[orthogonal]] axes. The model is regarded as a dimensional model of emotion.<ref>{{cite book | last = Evans | first = Dylan | author-link = Dylan Evans | title = Emotion A very short introduction | publisher = Oxford University Press | edition = 2nd
| date = 2019 | location = New York, USA | isbn = 978-0-19-883440-3}}</ref>

==Concepts==
The main concepts of the hypothesis are ''firstly'' that the monoamine neurotransmitters are [[Orthogonality#Chemistry and biochemistry|orthogonal variables]], meaning involving independent pairs of neurotransmitters; and ''secondly'' the proposed '''one-to-one relationship''' between the monoamine neurotransmitters and emotions.<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Vallverdú | first1 = Jordi | last2 = Müller | first2 = Vincent | title = Blended Cognition the Robotic Challenge | publisher = Springer Nature | series = Springer Series in Cognitive and Neural Systems | date = 2019 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-030-03104-6_1 | isbn = 978-3-030-03104-6 | s2cid = 150611062}}</ref>
